event.text: Starting with memory, since earlier incidents may change the plan for this supplier or its stores.

call.name: recall_memory
cypher:
MATCH (s:Supplier)-[:SUPPLIED]->(l:Lot {code: $lot})
OPTIONAL MATCH (l)-[:USED_IN|REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED*1..6]->(pl:ProductLot)
WITH s, collect(DISTINCT pl.sku) AS skus
WITH s, [(p:Product)-[:SHIPPED_UNTRACKED]->(a:Store) WHERE p.sku IN skus | a.id]
       + [(q:ProductLot)-[:SHIPPED_TO]->(b:Store) WHERE q.sku IN skus | b.id] AS stores
MATCH (m:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(x)
WHERE m.lot <> $lot AND (x = s OR (x:Store AND x.id IN stores))
RETURN m.lot AS from_lot, m.at AS at, labels(x)[0] AS kind, x.id AS about, m.fact AS fact
ORDER BY at DESC, about LIMIT 20

result.summary: I've proposed Class I at consumer depth, because this is Listeria monocytogenes in chilled ready-to-eat soups and sauces, and memory showed outbreak OB-2026-10 had already traced 6 of 6 cases to L-204. That confirmed outbreak is why I treated the hazard as serious from the start. Before anything else left the company, a hold stopped 93 kg of unused carrot at Northfield Plant 2 and 2,652 unshipped units at 2 plants and 3 distribution centres. The lot spread through batches B-03, B-05, B-07 and B-09 into 7 product lots and 31 stores, with B-03 as the main spread point because its leftovers were reworked into B-09. Two stores, ST-013 and ST-021, received Garden Vegetable Stew with no lot code recorded, memory showed no earlier lot-code problems at either, and the coordinator decided to pull it there too. The backward check found L-204 in none of the 8 product lots the 38 cleared stores received, so the scope holds: 33 stores to recall (31 traced, 2 with missing records) instead of a blanket 71, with 38 cleared and 2,256 units to pull. The class, releasing the hold and all 33 drafted notices still need the coordinator's approval; nothing has been sent.

lessons.fact: Valley Root Co. lot L-204 (diced carrot) carried Listeria monocytogenes, confirmed by supplier testing after outbreak OB-2026-10 linked 6 of 6 cases to it; it reached 31 stores via batches B-03, B-05, B-07, B-09.
B-03 was the top chokepoint for L-204 (betweenness 175, 16 stores downstream) because its leftovers were reworked into B-09.
ST-013 received 25 units of Garden Vegetable Stew (P-02) on 2026-10-09 with no lot code recorded during L-204; first time on record, and the coordinator pulled it.
ST-021 received 24 units of Garden Vegetable Stew (P-02) on 2026-10-10 with no lot code recorded during L-204; first time on record, and the coordinator pulled it.

cypher:
UNWIND $lessons AS lesson
MATCH (x {id: lesson.about}) WHERE x:Supplier OR x:Store OR x:Batch OR x:Site OR x:DC
CREATE (m:Memory {lot: $lot, fact: lesson.fact, at: $at})-[:ABOUT]->(x)
RETURN labels(x)[0] AS kind, x.id AS about, m.fact AS fact

notes.text: Starting with memory, since earlier incidents may change the plan for this supplier or its stores.
Memory shows outbreak OB-2026-10 already traced 6 of 6 cases to L-204, so the hazard is confirmed in people. I'm placing the hold now and proposing Class I at consumer depth together.
The hold covers 93 kg of raw carrot and 2,652 units across 5 locations. Next I'm tracing forward to find every store that received product.
The trace reached 31 stores through 4 batches, and B-03 was reworked into B-09. I'm ranking chokepoints and checking for gap stores at the same time.
B-03 is the top chokepoint, and its leftovers were reworked into B-09. Two stores received Garden Vegetable Stew with no lot code, so I'm asking the coordinator whether to pull it there.
The coordinator chose to pull, so I'm running the recall scope with the gap stores included.
The scope is 33 stores to recall and 38 cleared. I'm checking the cleared stores' 9 distinct lots backward, independently.
None of the 8 cleared lots contains L-204, so the scope holds. I'm drafting 33 notices and recording lessons.
